subject: Renewal: Expand Dedicated Pool to 32 GPUs — ratecard & throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@oxfordai.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@oxfordai.com>
Date: 2027-09-14 09:12 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation — expanding our reserved pool to 32 GPUs

Hi Naomi / Karthik,

Quick context: our renewal for the Dedicated cluster is coming up (Oct 1). We're planning to double our committed capacity from 16→32 GPUs to support a new multimodal service rolling into production. Before Procurement opens the redlines, can you confirm revised reserved rates (per GPU-hour) for a 12‑month renewal and any ramp / throughput SLOs you can offer?

Two asks from our side:
- A conservative per-hour committed rate (we typically want fixed unit economics for planning).
- A simple throughput guarantee (tail latency percentile for 8k tokens, per‑node throughput baseline) — if you have a short SLA matrix that would be great.

We may also need a small credit for the early commit — Procurement will push hard on that. Happy to jump on a quick call; otherwise send the proposed terms and we can route to legal.

Thanks,
Alex Reed
Head of Platform, OxfordAI
OxfordAI | alex.reed@oxfordai.com

Attachment: usage_snapshot_Q3.csv (referenced)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@oxfordai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-14 11:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — expanding our reserved pool to 32 GPUs

Alex — thanks for the clear asks.

High level: we can support the move to 32 GPUs on a 12‑month reserved term with a stepped ramp (16→24 on day 1 of the renewal; 24→32 after 60 days) or immediate 32 start if you need it. Below is the preliminary commercial framing; I'll loop in Dev for the technical SLA specifics.

Commercial proposal (preliminary):
- Committed term: 12 months (annual billing).
- Unit price (reserved GPU-hour): $2.20/hr (base) for 32‑GPU commit.
- Early renewal credit: one month of reserved capacity credited back if contract executed >30 days prior to renewal effective date.
- Volume discount: if you commit to 48 GPUs total across regions, price steps to $1.95/hr.

Operational notes:
- Throughput SLOs: we'll provide a short matrix (p50/p95/p99 token latency for 8k seq length; per-node throughput baseline) and can include a remediation credit for sustained breaches beyond the SLA window.
- Migration: we will coordinate a maintenance window for KV cache warmup and can offer prefix caching settings to reduce early tail latency.

I'll attach the updated ratecard and a draft amendment for your procurement team. Can you confirm OxfordAI's preferred start date (Oct 1 vs Oct 15) and whether you require immediate 32 GPU availability vs staged ramp?

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Reserved_Ratecard_v3.pdf; Draft_Amendment_OxfordAI.docx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 09:28 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal conversation — expand pool — need SLA numbers + engineering signoff

FYI — forwarding Alex's note. Need your help on two things, Dev:

1) Provide a compact SLA/throughput matrix we can hand to Procurement (p50/p95/p99 for 8k tokens; per-node throughput at 90% util). Keep it short, one slide or spreadsheet.
2) Confirm whether the staged ramp (16→24 day 1; 24→32 after 60 days) is safe for model performance and KV-cache warmup, or whether immediate 32 is recommended for OxfordAI's use-case.

If we can give a tight per-hour reserved rate that includes the reliability credit language, Procurement will move faster. Naomi — my sense is we can approve a one-time concession to $2.05/hr for the first 90 days if they sign by Sep 24 (covers their ask for an early-commit incentive). Need leadership sign-off but want to have the offer on paper.

-Karthik
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15 11:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal conversation — expand pool — need SLA numbers + engineering signoff

On Wed, Sep 15, 2027 at 09:28, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> FYI — forwarding Alex's note. Need your help on two things, Dev:
>
> 1) Provide a compact SLA/throughput matrix we can hand to Procurement (p50/p95/p99 for 8k tokens; per-node throughput at 90% util). Keep it short, one slide or spreadsheet.
> 2) Confirm whether the staged ramp (16→24 day 1; 24→32 after 60 days) is safe for model performance and KV-cache warmup, or whether immediate 32 is recommended for OxfordAI's use-case.

Short answers below — I'll follow up with the actual SLA matrix file.

- SLA / throughput (short):
  • 8k tokens, gpt-like model baseline on A100-equivalent nodes (multi tenancy factored): p50 = 18ms/token, p95 = 42ms/token, p99 = 120ms/token (these are averaged per token; convert to end-to-end for 8k seq).
  • Per-node steady-state throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec at 90% util for the workload shape in their snapshot.
  • Remediation: we propose a 5% monthly credit of reserved spend for sustained p99 breaches > 3 consecutive windows (we'll provide exact window definitions in the SLA doc).

- Ramp recommendation:
  • Staged ramp OK if they accept transient warmup degradation for rare long-context requests. KV cache hit-rate will take ~24–48 hours to stabilize after scale changes.
  • If OxfordAI needs predictable tail latency from day one, recommend immediate 32 GPU availability (we can reserve headroom and perform an orchestrated cache warmup).

Attaching a concise spreadsheet: throughput_sla_matrix.xlsx.

-Dev (for infra/serving)
Attachment: throughput_sla_matrix.xlsx

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@oxfordai.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@oxfordai.com>
Date: 2027-09-16 08:03 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — expanding our reserved pool to 32 GPUs

Thanks Naomi / Dev / Karthik — this is helpful. Procurement has two follow-ups:

1) Can Redwood make the early-execute credit unconditional if we sign by Sep 24 (we were hoping for the one-month credit without additional deliverables).
2) OxfordAI prefers immediate 32 GPU availability on day 1 due to traffic patterns. We'd accept a commitment to the immediate start plus a 60‑day stabilization SLA that limits remediation credits if issues are caused by their model changes.

On pricing: Procurement counters with $2.00/hr reserved for the 32 GPU commit, and asks whether Redwood can include a one‑time onboarding credit of $12,000 (applied as invoice credit) for migration support.

Can you confirm final best offer and I'll circulate to Procurement / Legal?

Best,
Alex
Attachment: procurement_terms_request.pdf

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@oxfordai.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-17 15:46 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — expanding our reserved pool to 32 GPUs

Alex — appreciate the clarity and the counter. Here's our finish-line proposal so you can take it to Procurement/Legal today: 

Commercial final: 
- Committed term: 12 months, immediate 32 GPUs effective on renewal effective date.
- Final unit price (reserved GPU-hour): $2.00/hr (applies for the full 12‑month term).
- One-time onboarding credit: $12,000 applied as invoice credit.
- Early-execute credit: unconditional one-month reserved capacity credit if the amendment is fully executed by 2027-09-24.

Operational / SLA: 
- OxfordAI gets the immediate 32 GPU start. We will run a coordinated cache warmup and validate p95/p99 using the provided snapshot during the first 72 hours.
- Stabilization window: 60 days where we will monitor and triage jointly. Remediation credits apply only for platform-side regressions (not for model-induced changes) per the SLA doc.

Next steps: I attached the updated ratecard and a clean draft amendment with the terms above (Draft_Amendment_OxfordAI.docx). If this matches Procurement's ask, we'll push the DocuSign link and target execution before 2027-09-24 to lock the early-execute credit.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/link/to/OXF-2027-amend
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/record/OXF-7890

If agreed, Procurement can sign and we'll set the migration and warmup runbook with Dev and Grace.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference
